craft_notes: Sthāyin: vīra of grasping; vyabhicāri utsāha at ends grasped. Sanskrit-first: vinaṣṭormicapalaḥ per UNC (kept); gṛhāṇa double (GRASP-ENDS ×2 — maintenance's end + my wandering's undoing, kept double). Rows: 9 (quit/dwell/show triple imperative — three acts, one breath), 1 (‘Lord’ closes — wandering's undoing addressed last). Close: ‘grasp ever my wandering state’s undoing, Lord’. Rupture: semicolon (dwelling stated, then its showing — quit/dwell, then show). Rejected: single grasp — killed: double grasps (two ends); ‘stillness’ for undivided — killed: akhaṇḍa kept. Read aloud: TO-quit OUT-er-WORK, TO-dwell IN-no-ble KNOW-ing-GROUND — … GRASP, god-DESS, MAIN-ten-ance's-END, THEN-grasp EV-er MY-wand-er-ing-STATE's un-DO-ing, LORD.

lines: To quit outer work, to dwell in noble knowing-ground —
show things undivided, waves gone fickle; grasp, goddess, maintenance's end, then grasp ever my wandering state's undoing, Lord.
l4.sanskrit_cite: bahir vṛttiṃ hātuṃ citibhuvam udārāṃ nivasituṃ | sthiteḥ sāṃsārikyāḥ kalayatu vināśaṃ mama sadā

reads_against.argmap: What shall the goddess grasp? → Quit outer, dwell noble, show undivided; grasp ends — maintenance's and mine.
c1_essence: Outer quit, noble dwelt, undivided shown; ends grasped.
